questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting, relevant and high-quality courses and teaching - particular focus on courses, that is unavailable at KU.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I struggled with some technical issues and STOP1 was very helpful, however it did require some persistency to actually fix the issues.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Housing is expensive in Australia and can be very difficult to find permanent housing. I used a facebook group called fairyfloss, which is what everyone uses and biggest recommendations. I found my room before travelling and have been in this same houseshare during my entire stay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Most houseshares will require that you sign onto the lease, this is completely normal, however make sure to read through the documents properly and know what you sign on to.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Mine was slightly unorthodox, as my birthday was registered wrongly. It was somewhat difficult to fix this issue, but the staff at UniMelb was very helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All you can imagine.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Best advice is to read thoroughly through your application.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Course load is higher, most classes had weekly assignments. Not very demanding or time consuming, but none the less more tasks, that is common at KU. However, my courses were not particularly theory-heavy and more case-oriented and critical.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All my courses were structured as seminars - fewer students, less lecturing and more in-class debate and participation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: "Human Rights", "Contemporary Middle East and South Asia", "Disaster and Humanitarian Aid", and "Conflict, Security and Development"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Disaster and humanitarian Aid was taught by Anne Decobért and Sutapa Chattopadhyay, who are an excellent educators.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I bought a bike, so transportation is one-time 1300DKK. Melbourne is bicycle friendly, however this is the only city in AUS, where I have found this to be the case. 
Be aware, that if you sign on to a lease of house, you are likely to pay a bond (depositum). 
Personal spending is difficult, bc it depends heavily on how many trips you go on. I saved a lot on food by going to markets and preparing most at home.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is expensive in Australia. Except for coffee at cafes, usually 5 AUD (20 DKK)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I dont know. I didnt partake in any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Make sure to go on some of the beautiful hikes around Melbourne. Grampians, Cathedral ranges, Great otway National Park, Wilsons Prom.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Roadtrip!! the nature inland and on the coasts are equallty fantastic and beautiful. Camping is the most economical (and also fun) method of travelling Australia. So if you are interested in this, consider bringing camping essentials from home, if you already own them. I regret not having brought I.e. headtorch, knife, sleeping mat etc. Many beautiful spots and hikes are only accessible with overnight hikes, which can feel so special :)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Melbourne is very european..

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Australians are so friendly :)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people here tend to be so welcoming and invite you along even if you've only just met.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Melbourne is actually pretty cold during winter, bring warm clothes.
2. Worth it trying to live in a sharehouse, even if it requires a bit of effort to find one. 
3. Dont underestimate how expensive it will be

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.answer: courses and nature

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: staying within budget...
